newsitem.title: USA: IBM reports solid second quarter results.
newsitem.headline: IBM reports solid second quarter results.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. Monday reported slightly higher earnings for the second quarter, as strong demand for its broad range of computer products and services offset lower sales of some hardware.

The world's largest computer maker said it earned $1.4 billion, or $1.46 a share, in the quarter, up from $1.3 billion, or $1.26 a share a year earlier, adjusted for a two-for-one stock split. The results were slightly higher than the Wall Street consensus estimate of $1.42 a share.
IBM's revenues rose 4 percent to $18.9 billion from $18.2 billion. Excluding changes in currency exchange rates, revenues climbed 8 percent, IBM said.

IBM said strong results in some businesses -- such as semiconductors, services and hard disk drives -- as well as improved results in mainframes, offset lower revenue in other segments, such as AS/400 minicomputers, RS/6000 workstations and consumer personal computers. IBM said the response to its new mainframe models was good.
IBM also described results from its commercial PCs and PC servers as "good."

"These results show the ongoing strength of our broad business portfolio," Chairman Louis Gerstner said in a statement. "We saw very good customer response to our new System/390 servers and continuing strength in services and hard disk drives."

IBM's revenues in North America grew 10 percent to $8.6 billion, Asia Pacific revenue rose 4 percent to $3.8 billion and Latin America grew 8 percent to $847 million. Revenues from Europe, the Middle East and Africa fell 5 percent to $5.7 billion.
Total hardware sales were flat at $8.6 billion.
Services revenues jumped 24 percent to $4.6 billion. About $3.3 billion in new services contracts were signed in the quarter and services continued to show strong growth, IBM said.
IBM stock fell 75 cents to $103.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. The company, based in Armonk, N.Y., reported results just after the close of trading.
